restated_question: After a 48-72 h TGF-beta1 pulse (2-5 ng/mL) and washout, primary human fibroblasts still show alpha-SMA stress fibres and contractility days later. Which experiments separate the possible maintainers - residual exogenous ligand, matrix-derived latent ligand, cell-to-cell signalling, a cell-intrinsic chromatin/TF state, mechanical self-reinforcement, senescence, population composition change, and measurement artefact - without assuming one of them and without assuming they exclude each other?

objectives.statement: Decide whether the persisting phenotype requires ongoing TGF-beta receptor input after washout.
If input is required, identify its source: carried-over exogenous ligand, matrix latent TGF-beta, or cell-secreted factors.
Test cell-intrinsic routes: chromatin/TF memory, senescence, and mechanical self-reinforcement including substrate stiffness.
Determine whether persistence is a per-cell state change or a change in population composition.
Establish that the readouts measure what they are taken to measure: ligand detection limit, blocker efficacy, alpha-SMA protein turnover.
Determine which interventions reverse the phenotype and on what timescale.

sub_questions.question: Does the persisting phenotype require continued TGF-beta receptor signalling after washout?

Is senescence part of the persisting phenotype?
Is persistence a property of individual cells or of the population?
Could the apparent persistence be produced by the measurement itself?

experiments.design: PRIORITY. Washout quality, ligand measurement and blockade-timing in one plate layout. Primary human fibroblasts (3 donors, passage 3-5, matched seeding density, 1% serum from 24 h before the pulse) are treated with recombinant TGF-beta1 5 ng/mL for 72 h, then washed out (3 x PBS rinse, then 2 full medium changes 2 h apart, then fresh TGF-beta1-free medium). Arms carried from the moment of washout: (a) vehicle; (b) pan-TGF-beta neutralising antibody 1D11 10 ug/mL continuous, with isotype IgG control; (c) TGF-beta-RI kinase inhibitor SB431542 10 uM continuous, with DMSO control; (d) SB431542 added only from day 3 (delayed-block arm); (e) never-treated cells handled identically; (f) CELL-FREE wells pulsed and washed exactly like (a) with no cells, to measure what the plastic and the medium alone give back; (g) naive cells challenged acutely with 5 ng/mL TGF-beta1 in the presence of each blocker, as the blocker-efficacy control; (h) medium spiked with 10 pg/mL TGF-beta1 as assay spike-recovery. Medium is sampled at 6 h, day 1, day 3 and day 5 after washout; cells are fixed at day 1, 3 and 5.

experiments.priority_rationale: It is first because it is the only experiment that measures the washout itself rather than assuming it, and because the pack contains no source that measures residual exogenous TGF-beta1 - the weakest link in every later interpretation. It also carries both measurement-assumption checks, and its result reorders everything after it: if residual ligand or ongoing receptor signalling is present, the intrinsic-state experiments would be run on a culture that is still being driven. After reading: a fibroblast pulse-washout study reports persistence with ongoing pSmad2/3 attributed to autocrine TGF-beta1, so whether the ligand after washout is carried over or newly made decides how every later blockade result is read. Blockade cannot tell the two apart, and TGFB1 mRNA may not either (autoinduction), so E1 adds a latent-form readout as a candidate, with its own dose check, and a pSmad2 time course.

experiments.design: Conditioned-medium transfer and co-culture, to test whether anything the treated cells release is sufficient to install or maintain the phenotype in naive cells. Donor cells: pulsed and washed as in E1. Conditioned medium is collected over 24 h windows ending at day 3 and day 5 after washout, centrifuged and sterile-filtered, then applied to naive fibroblasts (same donor and passage) for 72 h, with and without 1D11 10 ug/mL. Parallel arms: transwell co-culture of washed-out cells above naive reporter cells (no contact), and direct mixed co-culture with the naive population pre-labelled (CellTracker or a lentiviral marker) so donor and recipient can be scored apart. Control media: CM from never-treated cells collected on the same schedule, and medium conditioned in cell-free pulsed-and-washed wells, which carries carryover ligand but no cell product.

evidence.statement: Reversible and irreversible differentiation of cardiac fibroblasts.

locator.source_text:
Aims

Differentiation of cardiac fibroblasts (Fbs) into myofibroblasts (MyoFbs) is responsible for connective tissue build-up in myocardial remodelling. We examined MyoFb differentiation and reversibility.

Methods and results

Adult rat cardiac Fbs were cultured on a plastic substratum providing mechanical stress, with conditions to obtain different levels of Fb differentiation. Fb spontaneously differentiated to proliferating MyoFb (p-MyoFb) with stress fibre formation decorated with alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA). Transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) promoted differentiation into α-SMA-positive MyoFb showing near the absence of proliferation, i.e. non-p-MyoFb. SD-208, a TGF-β-receptor-I (TGF-β-RI) kinase blocker, inhibited p-MyoFb differentiation as shown by stress fibre absence, low α-SMA expression, and high proliferation levels. Fb seeded in collagen matrices induced no contraction, whereas p-MyoFb and non-p-MyoFb induced 2.5- and four-fold contraction. Fb produced little collagen but high levels of interleukin-10. Non-p-MyoFb had high collagen production and high monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 and tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases-1 levels.

evidence.statement: Reversible and irreversible differentiation of cardiac fibroblasts.

locator.source_text:
Transcriptome analysis indicated differential activation of gene networks related to differentiation of MyoFb (e.g. paxilin and PAK) and reduced proliferation of non-p-MyoFb (e.g. cyclins and cell cycle regulation). Dedifferentiation of p-MyoFb with stress fibre de-polymerization, but not of non-p-MyoFb, was induced by SD-208 despite maintained stress. Stress fibre de-polymerization could also be induced by mechanical strain release in p-MyoFb and non-p-MyoFb (2-day cultures in unrestrained 3-D collagen matrices). Only p-MyoFb showed true dedifferentiation after long-term 3-D cultures.

Conclusions

Fb, p-MyoFb, and non-p-MyoFb have a distinct gene expression, ultrastructural, and functional profile. Both reduction in mechanical strain and TGF-β-RI kinase inhibition can reverse p-MyoFb differentiation but not non-p-MyoFb.

locator.source_text: Myofibroblasts are critical for connective tissue remodeling and wound healing since they can close wound beds and shape tissues rapidly by generating high traction forces and secreting abundant extracellular matrix proteins and matrix metalloproteinases. However, their presence in excessive numbers is associated with fibrotic and calcific diseases and tissue thickening in engineered tissues. While activation of the myofibroblast phenotype has been studied extensively, whether myofibroblasts are "cleared" by phenotypic reversal or by apoptosis remains controversial. The goal of this work is to test the hypothesis that mechanical inhibition of myofibroblast force generation leads to de-differentiation or apoptosis depending upon the magnitude of the decrease in tension. To test this hypothesis, we cultured valvular interstitial cells (VICs) in fibrin micro-tissues suspended between flexible posts and dynamically altered the ability of the cells to generate tension by altering boundary stiffness via magnetic forces applied to posts. The flexible posts capped with magnetic beads enable the measurement and modulation of tension generated by the cells within the tissue. As expected, the

evidence.statement: Simultaneous induction of differentiation and senescence in cardiac fibroblasts by TGF-β1: effects of senotherapeutics drugs.

locator.source_text:
Introduction

Aging is a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases (CVD), partly due to the accumulation of senescent cells. Senescence is characterized by irreversible cell cycle arrest and the acquisition of a senescence associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which promotes inflammation and tissue remodeling, thereby contributing to cardiac dysfunction. Cardiac fibroblasts (CFs), key regulators of cardiac repair, differentiate into myofibroblasts (CMFs) in response to pathological stimuli such as mechanical stiffness and TGF-β1. CMFs secrete abundant extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins, and while their senescence may transiently restrict fibrosis in acute cardiac injury, persistent senescence promotes chronic remodeling through SASP activity. Given that TGF-β1 is a central mediator of CF-to-CMF differentiation and can induce senescence in various cell lines, we investigated whether it simultaneously triggers both processes in neonatal rat CFs, and whether the senotherapeutics Navitoclax and Dasatinib + Quercetin modulate the viability of senescent CMFs.

Methods

CF from neonatal rats were incubated in DMEM-F12 (10% FBS), and treated with TGF-β1 (10 46 ng/mL, 7

CFs treated with TGF-β1 exhibited senescence markers (p15-p16, p21), increased SA-β-gal activity, and reduced Ki-67 and p-Rb expression. CMFs displayed enhanced secretion of IL-1β, IL-6, IL-5, and IL-10, together with elevated collagen and VCAM-1 levels, indicating a pro-fibrotic and low-grade inflammatory phenotype. evidence.statement: Dupuytren's Disease Is Mediated by Insufficient TGF-β1 Release and Degradation.

locator.source_text: Dupuytren's disease (DD) is a fibroproliferative disorder affecting the palmar fascia, causing functional restrictions of the hand and thereby limiting patients' daily lives. The disturbed and excessive myofibroblastogenesis, causing DD, is mainly induced by transforming growth factor (TGF)-β1. But, the extent to which impaired TGF-β1 release or TGF-β signal degradation is involved in pathologically altered myofibroblastogenesis in DD has been barely examined.
